utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two short matters, please. First, just simply to bring the Chamber and Defence counsel up to date on rebuttal, we attempted to file at the end of last week a first document setting out our rebuttal position as it is currently known to be. Unfortunately, some of the documents were in B/C/S and, therefore, filing of the document was refused. We've withdrawn the B/C/S documents from the filing, and I think we'll refile that document today. But I hope the Chamber will accept that we're doing all we can to keep everybody informed at the earliest possible moment of what the intended rebuttal position is. Second thing concerns the Cerkez witnesses. I have a letter dated the 30th of August setting out the witnesses for this week. Two problems: one, a comparatively slight one, that, of course, whether there's a complete reversal of order of witnesses makes life a little more difficult, but I do understand the difficulties that counsel will be facing. Second, at least two of these witnesses were not on the original witness list of the Defence. That's the first witness to be called, Ivica Markovic, who was first notified as a potential witness on the 22nd of August of this year. Then I think that number 4 was not on any of the earlier lists, going back to April, and likewise number 7. The Chamber will recall the approach that was taken to any additions of witnesses on our lists. Indeed, we were excluded witnesses simply on the grounds that they weren't on the original list. I'm not making any particular point myself about witnesses not being on the list because I'm not here to obstruct in any way. But it may be the Chamber would want to be alerted to the fact that witnesses weren't on an earlier list; it may, because it's the Chamber's Rules that require witnesses to be listed, require from the Defence some explanation for why these witnesses are added late. Of course, it's important that I draw these matters to your attention so that if, in due course, there are any further arguments about witnesses being called not subject of early notification, perhaps witnesses in rebuttal, a general even-handedness of treatment can be borne in mind. My understanding, therefore, is that numbers 1, 3, and 7 were not the subject of any earlier notification before, at the very earliest, the 22nd of August; that is, last week. The Chamber will also recall that so far as affidavit witnesses are concerned, affidavit witnesses are now, I think, regularly allowed in without being on witness lists of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic, that seems to be a reasonable complaint. What is the answer? There may come a time when we are not able to allow witnesses to be called because they haven't been notified. The Rules are not there to be flouted, they're there to be obeyed. I'm also troubled by the extensive nature of the witnesses you propose to call, the considerable number, and the implications for timing, because, of course, you know that your case has to finish by that week in October. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, some changes in witness lists are the product of the request of the Court to cut the number of witnesses down. That is one reason. Then we took a number of steps to replace some witnesses, that is, to bring in some other witnesses who could testify about two or three topics, and that is why we changed it. We did find them. But that meant that we had to bring in some new witnesses. But these new witnesses are now standing in for perhaps as many as four or five other witnesses each. The second reason -- and that is the number of new names as against the first list. The second reason is that, unfortunately, the disclosure of new documents in this case go on even as the second Defence took up its case. We are still receiving very many new documents from the Prosecution. I'm not talking about exceptions, about a few documents, but about a very large number of documents. These documents contain a great deal of information which we did not have at our disposal during the Prosecutor's case. It is difficult to say whether some of this evidence could be left for rebuttal, that is, rejoinder, because simply that is not specified by the Rules. We think that while we are presenting our case, and as long as we are finding out new facts from new material that we are getting, that we can still adjust our Defence to that. As for the time that you asked about, after two or three weeks we shall try to see where we are. We have very little reserve. Some of the witnesses in the last list, and that has been significantly cut down, are, in a manner of speaking, standby witnesses, reserve witnesses, and if the other witnesses provide us with enough material, then perhaps we shall be able to strike some of them out. If I may remind the Court, earlier during Kordic's Defence, we discussed the disclosure of new documents by the Prosecution. We did apply flexibility, especially since we had to move our Defence two weeks, a fortnight, ahead, as against the earlier plan. So these are basically the problems that we have to face up to. I should like to tell Your Honours that if there were no new disclosures, then we would have stood by our old list and we could say that three witnesses from our earlier lists are now replaced by one witness, and that will be it. Unfortunately, in view of the present situation, we cannot do it. But I should like to assure you that we are trying to behave as rationally as possible and that we do not intend to bring up any new evidence except for reasons which are basic, which are highly material to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's up to you how you conduct your Defence, except that you must give notice of witnesses, proper notice. And also we shall expect you to finish on time, Mr. Kovacic. It may be that you will want to review at the end of this week the order of witnesses or the number of witnesses you call each week in order that we can call more and thus get through them. But let us begin now and get on. Your first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our first witness today will be Mr. Ivica Markovic. He will be testifying about the developments in Novi Travnik. In Cerkez's indictment, Count 2, persecution, he is charged for the municipalities of Vitez, Novi Travnik, and Busovaca. With this witness, we intend to round off the Novi Travnik charge. We already had a witness before the break about Novi Travnik and Cerkez's position while he was in Novi Travnik. This will be the second witness who will testify about it from another angle. Following that, there will be no new witnesses about Novi Travnik. So I should like to call the witness, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Markovic, take a seat. Examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Court your name, your date of birth, your place of birth, for the record.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I am Ivica Markovic. I was born on the 7th of June 1947 in Kiseljak, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Markovic, are you married? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I am married and father of three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your education, what kind of education do you have?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the High School of Commerce at the Faculty of Political Sciences, Defence and Protection, and the high coaching -- school in football coaching.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Department of National Defence was part of the Faculty of Political Sciences in Sarajevo, was it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, where did you work, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, I worked for the Bratstvo company in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bratstvo company in Novi Travnik was -- is the largest employer in Novi Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is, and Novi Travnik began to grow as a town after the Bratstvo company was founded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the order of magnitude that we are talking about, what was the staff of Bratstvo as we speak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There are about 7.000 people employed by the Bratstvo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when the company's good at working, that the town is alive and well?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is quite true because there was no other branch of industry there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, I should now like to move on to the post you held in 1992 and 1993. Tell the Court, please, when were you the commander of the municipality staff of the HVO in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I was its commander since its establishment until August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, you were assigned to another post?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, I was the head of the defence office in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And towards the end of the war, you held a third post, is it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of the war in 1993, I moved to the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade to become the head of the department for operational affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in September 1993 until after the Washington Accords?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What you have just told us it transpires -- no, let me rephrase it. Is it then correct that this municipal HVO staff in Novi Travnik was set up sometime in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not become the commander on the first day, there was another man for a short while; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was Jozo Ljubas for about ten days, and then I took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of your academic degree and your earlier experience, you were qualified for the job; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Since we didn't have any active duty military with the professional military education.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, at that time when the HVO staff was set up, what was its purpose? Why was the staff established?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The staff was established as a body bringing together the Croat people against the Serb aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, was it only the Croat people which defended Bosnia against the Serb aggression or were there others too?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. At that time, both the Muslim and the Croat peoples defended Bosnia against the Serb aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were engaged in that defence together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Muslim people, did they have an organisation for the defence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They inherited the Territorial Defence staff. That name, that is the Territorial Defence from the former system, and there was a coordination between those two bodies. There was regular coordination between those two bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A couple of words within that context about parties. Were the strongest and largest political parties in Novi Travnik were the HDZ and the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other parties played a minor role?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SDA rallied what ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The SDA rallied the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Croat people?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Croat Democratic Union rallied the Croat people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In early 1992, and even before that, those two political parties had different views on the prospects of war which then struck Bosnia. Could you tell us in a couple of words what was the difference between them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, the Muslim people did not think that there would be an aggression and that the JNA would attack Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, the Croat people, following the events in Croatia, realised that would not be the end of the war and that the aggression would spill over into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your view, was that why the HZ HB encouraged the establishment of municipal staffs?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Municipal staffs also discharged a civilian faction in terms of the organisation of defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And traditionally in our system, it was the matter for civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, they also performed the military functions; that is, they formed units for the defence against this aggression. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: A goodish part of units had already been set up as village guards in villages, and we tried to put them together and direct them to the right place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, were you a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I was never a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But a similar job to yours in the Novi Travnik staff, that is, there was a similar organisation in other municipalities, neighbouring municipalities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Marijan Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Marijan Skopljak because he held the same post as I did in Vitez, and in Travnik it was late Ivica -- his last name escapes me. He died in the combat -- oh, yes, Stojak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned village guards, but we shall come back to that later. At that time, in the early days of the defence organisation in Novi Travnik on both sides with one and the other people, could you tell us who was the commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence was Saban Mandzuka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did he leave the TO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Saban Mandzuka left the Territorial Defence, that is, that particular post after the first conflict in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first conflict in Novi Travnik was when?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean June 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in a couple of words why did Saban Mandzuka leave the head post in the TO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Saban Mandzuka worked with me, because in the earlier term of office, 1982 to 1986, I was the TO commander and he was the commander of operations. When I talked to Saban, he said he did not want to fight against the Croat people and that that was not his war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this mean, in your view, that the extremist forces on the Muslim side took over the leadership and that was why Saban left?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by those who succeeded him, yes, you could say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after Saban, for a short period of time there was another man who commanded the TO in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: For a short time, it was Harbas Zuhdija. Before that, he was the commander of the Stojkovici base. And that summer, he was succeeded by Refik Lendo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Refik Lendo was a professional soldier, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Refik Lendo came from the JNA as a professional.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he from the area, was he native to that area, or did he come from outside?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. He came from the area. He came from Drenica but he arrived during the preparations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another time when he was assigned to that post, he did not live there, he had just come back?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had come back, but his family stayed back in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned village guards. Shall we try to explain those village guards. Who established the village guards, or rather, why were they formed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Every village formed its village guards. They patrolled villages at night and protected villages against bandits and marauders who appeared at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the village guards at that time, for reasons that you mentioned, that at that time, Bosnia, the state, failed to discharge its state functions?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, the state has ceased to function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village guards, were they also set up because there was still JNA units in the area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of Novi Travnik, there were JNA units both at the Stojkovici base and at Slimena and on Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The municipal staff that we talked about, that is, the staff in Novi Travnik, did it have any command role over those village guards?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: We were just trying to set this up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in a couple of sentences what was the rub? Why is it that you were trying? Does it mean that you failed or what?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, every village was a state unto itself. Everybody wanted to defend only his own village, and our problem was the front against the Serbs, to the JNA, which was in the neighbourhood. So we had problems with replenishing some front lines because they were saying, "I shall defend my village." But the village is not defended in the village; sometimes it has to be defended five or ten kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Markovic, in a manner of speaking, could we say that the organisation of village guards by the force of inertia was merely the continuation of the concept of All National Defence of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was the consternation of that concert, because village guards were established in all villages around Novi Travnik regardless of the population in them. In a number of cases, they were even mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no doubt in your mind whatsoever that they were self-organised.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that is quite certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you organised units for concrete actions. We already mentioned that. How did you and your staff form those units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we would call the commander of a village and tell him, "Give us five, six, ten men, because we have to replenish the unit to face the JNA," and they would assign five or ten men; sometimes by force, sometimes some would refuse. And after completing the task, they would go back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the command, you also at some point started developing mobilisation lists which at first you did not have; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At first there were no lists. But Mr. Senkic then arrived in the command and I tasked him with keeping a notebook of the volunteers who were coming daily to offer their services for the homeland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was from those lists that you were calling people for certain operations.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you called him, such a person would become a soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when he was given a task. And he was also provided with food and other provisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the task had been carried out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Then they would go back home. The Bratstvo factory at that time was not working very much anymore, and people just stayed and worked at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that when a person would come back from a certain operation, back to his village, would this person now be a civilian again?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: He was free during that period. He was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would have been a matter of his own decision whether he would join a fishing club or a chess club or go and do something else?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Until his next shift came up, he was free to do whatever he wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should save some time. This system was in force even later when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, during the war of 1992/1993, in Novi Travnik there were several significant conflicts between the Muslim and Croat ethnic groups. How many major conflicts were there during that period?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: During that period there were three conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should clarify. When did the first interethnic conflict take place? Was it a real conflict or was it just a more serious incident?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I would call it a limited incident because it was limited to only several hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What caused this incident?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, the barricades were erected on the road leading to Bratstvo, and a second barricade was also set up on our part near the town. I went to Mr. Mandjuka and we agreed that they both be dismantled by 11.00 and that free passage be allowed. That was done. Then I was informed that our flag had been taken down from the TO command building, where we had our joint police forces. I asked Mr. Mandjuka to order the flag taken back and he could not do it. And then there was a conflict. No HVO forces were involved; only the HOS forces were involved in this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first mentioned the order in which the barricades were erected, who was the first to have erected the barricade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Muslims because it was their neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you responded to that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flags which you mentioned, were those the usual flags, flags used at the time, or were they especially provocative?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer. We only had those flags. Those were the usual flags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in regard to this first conflict, you mentioned HOS. Was the HOS at that time within the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were an independent unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, was HOS a monoethnic force?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, there were also Muslims within the HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Insofar as you knew at the time, how many Muslims were there? Only a couple of them or many?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There were several of them. Those were Muslims who had been fighting in Croatia and had come back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when the second conflict in Travnik took place?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the second conflict took place in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what caused that conflict?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The cause of that conflict was a gas station which was directly behind the HVO headquarters, near the old hotel. The Muslims wanted us to turn it over to them so that they could use it, even though we told them that there was another station on the edge of town. And we wanted to reach an agreement so that both sides could use both stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that each side used one of the gas stations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They were on both ends of the town, and until that time, one could freely use both of them. The amount of fuel was limited, but both sides could use it if the proper orders were issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a general regulation that affected all population?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this attack on the gas station was led by a person who was known in the area by the nickname of Sosa?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he was born in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Drenica is part of the Novi Travnik municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but towards Opara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's been no evidence yet of any attack. All the witness has said is that the conflict was caused by a Muslim demand that they have the use of a gas station. Now, the witness should tell us, before we go on to anybody leading an attack, what happened. Now, Mr. Markovic, will you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: This gas station could not be turned over for their use because then we would have had to move our headquarters from this old hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The LiveNote is not working. We're not getting a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, we have a problem with the technology. Mr. Kovacic, if you'd like to take a seat --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- while we try and sort this out. Are we on line? THE COURT REPORTER: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, you said that the gas station couldn't be turned over. Then tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, in the evening, an attack on the headquarters ensued with the objective to take control of it, and also the radio relay facility up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so to clarify, who carried out the attack?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, what was the result of this conflict? How did it end, and what was the situation following this conflict?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: This conflict lasted for about seven days, until the ceasefire was finally established. What it resulted in was the definitive division of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a line of separation established, and both sides, the Croat and the Muslim, controlled one part of the town.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this division, if I may call it that, under whose control did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Bratstvo factory stay?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It remained under the Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croats, then, had no more access to it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After the negotiations which followed that conflict, for a period of time there were still mixed security units; that is, there was a professional unit that was still going on for awhile. And after that, the access was denied even to those employees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, who managed to negotiate this ceasefire, and how did that happen?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: From what I knew as the head of the HVO headquarters, it was Mr. Blaskic, and Mr. Merdan, the Muslim commander in Zenica. That is who we got our orders from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the ceasefire was reached by the military structures at the higher level or at the level of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether the negotiations were conducted at the level of the civilian structures. We couldn't negotiate. There was fear. Since there were dead and wounded involved, we all tried very hard to keep up the ceasefire, which was finally established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the ceasefire was established, how long did it last? In other words, when did the third conflict take place in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The third conflict followed in 1993. I believe it was in June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that conflict break out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: For awhile we had a joint line at Kamenjas and Slatke Voda against the JNA army in Donji Vakuf. Then before the conflict, the Muslims pulled out their forces. We had to spread out in order to cover the entire sector. Before the actual conflict, there was a village of Senkovici which was mixed. We were denied access to it, we were unable to talk to them, and then several days later an overall attack against Novi Travnik followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this operation, the ABiH gained control over other Croat villages in that area around town.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to Senkovici, Margitici, and the village of Pecine, which was under the ABiH control, and our unit which held the line against the JNA at Kamenjas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kamenjas was part of a front line north-west of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is in the Bugojno/Donji Vakuf sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of all this, Mr. Markovic, regardless of the front line against the JNA but both forces stayed on that front line, isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After the third conflict, our unit pulled out across the Serb-held territory, they surrendered to the Serbs. It was forced by the ABiH and then ABiH took over that part of the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was only in June of 1993 that the HVO completely abandoned that part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you said, this front line was abandoned due to betrayal of the -- of your then partners?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They -- that is the solution that they decided on. The communication lines at that time had been cut off and decisions were made such as were made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus you on the period between the second and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. third conflicts between October 1992 and June 1993. Did it hold, this cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: More or less it did. Free movement was able. One needed permissions, but there were no major obstacles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the organised forces and the civilian structures of the HVO and the BiH army, did those two armed forces ever have confrontation during that period?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any incidents in the town itself, criminal incidents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Such occurrences were -- several, and we tried to prevent them. There was a murder of an ethnic Muslim, another one was beaten up. Those were incidents and we disciplined those who committed those offences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, the victims were members of both ethnic groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Thieves usually don't take into account ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can assume that the perpetrators were also members of both ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was mixed even though, in our area, there were very few Muslim perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can I please ask the usher to help me show the witness Exhibit number D1/2. Mr. Markovic, please take a look at this. Tell me, is this the event that you just mentioned, or rather, is this one of the events that we talked about?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the events that occurred in Novi Travnik; however, I have to note that Juka, Zoran Jukic, nicknamed Juka, rather, before that tried to rape one of our little girls. Before the war, he had a criminal record. He did time in gaol, he was not a member. He was a member of HOS but then he was kicked out of there too. So he was a freelancer so to speak. He did not belong to a single unit, but what the document says is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know that during this incident a member of the military police regrettably, when trying to take into custody this well-known bandit Juka, did not manage to arrest him but had to shoot him?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He offered resistance and therefore they had to shoot him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this piece of news carried on local radio?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the range of these radios was as it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When speaking of extremists in this area, is it true that in the area of town, or rather in the immediate vicinity of town, there were also Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we encountered the Mujahedin later during the third conflict. They were stationed in Mehuric near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the area that they moved in?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the area that they moved in. They did not enter the lower part of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The centre?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to finish with this third conflict, I would like D72/2 to be shown to the witness, please. Mr. Markovic, please take a look at this graph. Could you also give us your comments? Is it correct that this irregular red line to the left of the words "Novi Travnik" is practically the line of separation between the Muslim and the Croat forces in Novi Travnik after the second conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let us be quite clear on this. The HVO retained its presence only in this right-hand upper corner of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the line of separation after the second conflict and that's the way it remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't put this question clearly. Could you please show the boundaries of the municipality with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all of this is the area of the municipality of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please show us which part you kept, only that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your right, the next municipality, is that Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To the left is Travnik and to the right is Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During this same period, that is to say, between the second and third conflict, that is to say, between October 1992 and June 1993, that is to say, until you lost that part of the sector, it was the Serbs that you mentioned. A line was held against the JNA Strikanci, Kamenjas, Slatka Vode, whatever the names are?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had divided sectors there. One part was kept by the BH army and the other by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you coordinated your activities in this respect?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier on in 1992, was there cooperation in terms of the procurement of weapons and distribution of weapons when action was taken against the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certain resources were taken from the Bratstvo factory and were distributed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, evenly, evenly. That is to say mortars and other weapons that were manufactured by Bratstvo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we say that the BH army and the HVO were equally supplied from this source?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But there were also some illegal entries into Bratstvo during the night, and I cannot ascertain who did this because until before the war, I was commander of this civilian defence of Bratstvo, this protection force of Bratstvo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So actually these burglaries and thefts started before the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the HVO was set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we conclude this by hearing an assessment from you. You are a participant in these events. There was a conflict between the Croats and the Muslims. What was the basic reason for these conflicts? Why was there all of a sudden a conflict between these two nationalities in that area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this happened because of the large number of refugees that arrived in the territory of Novi Travnik and this had disturbed the ethnic balance. People were simply afraid that a certain ethnic group would prevail. Then there were also the Mujahedin who did various things in Travnik and also went to the front lines and carried out provocations there. Then there were the refugees from Krajina. Lots of them came to Travnik. The Serbs expelled them, and probably with a certain intention in mind to disturb the ethnic balance. And I think that one of the reasons for the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims is the disruption of this ethnic balance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, there were less and less resources; is that right? Supplies from the surrounding republics, notably Croatia, became increasingly difficult?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all resources were limited from any point of view. It was difficult to bring in supplies, and this is one of the reasons why the larger population that came to exist required greater supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. When was the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade founded, can you tell us that, and on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established in December 1992 at the order of Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was an intermunicipal brigade of the HVO, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was the only intermunicipal HVO brigade in Central Bosnia because simply at that time there were not enough men to establish an independent brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Intermunicipal means belonging to two municipalities. Which are these two municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: This was a joint brigade for the municipality of Vitez and Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All other municipalities in Central Bosnia managed to establish their very own brigades; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, who was the first commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The first commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was Mr. Boro Malbasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when Malbasic was commander, was Mario Cerkez in the command and which post did he hold, if any?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mario Cerkez was in the brigade and, as far as I know, he was chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "chief of staff", you mean chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And ex officio, at the same time, he is deputy commander of the brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the beginning of February 1993, Malbasic was transferred to Vares? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he never returned to Novi Travnik; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time, Mario Cerkez was appointed temporary commander?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when was the decision passed or, rather, the order that every municipality had to have its own brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think this was in March 1993 because it was simply difficult to agree on -- to agree on how supplies could be procured for different municipalities, and that was probably one of the reasons why it was decided to establish separate brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apropos while Cerkez was a member of the command and in fact commander from December to March, the period that we are discussing, you communicated with him being head of the defence department, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At meetings of the civilian department of the HVO, the government of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which questions did you cooperate with Cerkez bearing in mind your office?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, mainly about manning the brigade and also obtaining material technical resources, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of these contacts, could you conclude that this was one of Cerkez's assignments in the command that he was supposed to provide for the support of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of these contacts, do you also know that at the same time, Cerkez communicated with your mentioned colleague, Marijan Skopljak, for the same purpose?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: We seldom had contacts, and by the very logic of matters, he would always say at government meetings that after that, he would go to Vitez to discuss the same matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anything change by way of substance in the relations between the defence department and the brigade, the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, when Cerkez became commander of this brigade, when from being number two, he became number one?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the transfer wasn't really felt. He simply had less time to drop by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that, at that time, the brigade had a sector of defence against the JNA in the mountains to the north-west of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This activity was carried out regularly and in an organised fashion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the way it had to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade had two battalions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they manned in relation to territories since you covered two municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: One battalion was provided by the Novi Travnik municipality whereas the other battalion was provided by the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any permanent members of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was the command of the brigade and also logistics, the supporting staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military staff, as far as going to the lines was concerned, how was this organised?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They were called up from their homes and there was a certain collection point and, from there, they were sent to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the brigade have any accommodation facilities of their own where the military would be stationed, like barracks?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There wasn't any such thing in the part of the municipality of Novi Travnik that was under our control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this military conscript would return from the front line, was he still a soldier while at home?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: He would be free until he were called up again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we mentioned that before so let's not go back to all of that. The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as opposed to the situation that you had, did they have barracks and did they have permanent members of their military?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In the territory of Novi Travnik, the situation was the same with the BH army as it was with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as regards the wider territory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The barracks in Travnik was BH army barracks and -- well, Zenica, I don't know about, so I can't really give you more extensive answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a barracks?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is now used by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any problems with recruiting these men, with calling them up in terms of numbers, in terms of their ability?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There were every day problems both in terms of call up and in terms of their ability.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes mobilise men who were above military age?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Men who, according to the old law, were not eligible were actually being mobilised, and we even took in disabled men who had volunteered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just a small matter by way of illustration. If a military conscript whom you sent call-up papers to would not appear, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which period you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Tomasevic period, that is to say, until March.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, we would address a request to the military police and then the military police would bring this military conscript in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the military police be able to carry this out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, for the most part, unless this person was in hiding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that, the staff in 1992, what would happen if somebody would refuse to report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he would be criticised by his co-villagers. But otherwise we couldn't do, really, anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it means regardless of the existence of summons, at that time in 1992, one reported if he wanted to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But we mostly summoned people who were on the volunteer list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they had reported themselves because they wanted to be called.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In those contacts at the Stjepan Tomasevic time, did you, with Mario Cerkez or Borivoj Malbasic before that, did you learn anything about the military task of Cerkez regarding the organisation of front lines?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Borivoj Malbasic said that Mario had to be in touch with me specially regarding the engineering works on the front line there, up towards Kamenjas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The engineering works on the front line, he evidently needed some support, that is, the machinery, materiel, so on and so forth, and the municipality tried to provide it to him.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the municipality tried to provide it, but we mostly did it manually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Markovic, you were a member of the civilian, subsequently military structure of the HVO throughout the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you know if there was ever any policy or command or order or a document, a request, put to us formally or informally to persecute Muslim civilians, to harass them, that they are perhaps second-class citizens or anything?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about such orders, and I claim here under full responsibility that I simply would not have been able to carry out such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there was some informal policy in that direction, would you have known about it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in view of the number of Muslims who had stayed behind in Novi Travnik after the first conflict, I believe I would have known about this because we were neighbours. As a matter of fact, I protected them there throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You took part in the various negotiations, resolution of incidents in 1992 and 1993. You even mentioned some of those specifically. You also had access to information regarding the developments, that is, refugees exchanged, the wounded, so on and so forth. You were wise to all these matters.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of the story, now that one looks at all these facts together, could you tell us which people was most victimised in your area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: My opinion is that both peoples were victimised equally in the area of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of the number of refugees, do you remember which people had more refugees?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, I can speak only about Novi Travnik which was under our control, we had some 20.000 refugees from Travnik and neighbouring villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Croats.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Croats. But I couldn't really tell you about the upper part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. We showed this on the map so I'm not going back to that. But from the end of April 1993, when the Vitez Brigade had already separated, did the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade have along its flanks any contact with the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: We had contact with the Vitez Brigade at Lazine, Zaselje. And when necessary, we sent some replenishments for the Vitez Brigade to the area of Zabrdze.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is where Gradina is too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These replenishments, what it really meant was that these brigades would step in depending on the necessity, depending on the pressure to cover the weak spots, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It changed from one case to another depending on what we needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But basically the interface of the two brigades was the municipal boundaries; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you are telling us are exceptions from one case to another.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To conclude, Mr. Markovic, your plans before that unfortunate war, were you planning to stay in Novi Travnik all your life?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I came to Novi Travnik when I was 35 and I thought that was the last station in my life. I was planning to grow old there, and to die there probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point, you evacuated your family to Rijeka, to Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1992 I evacuated my family, when the JNA aircraft was flying at supersonic speed. Then I realised what would happen and I evacuated my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I guess you were not the only one in the town who did that. It was an all-round phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, everybody did that. All those who had wives and children, they took them away. And we stayed behind to fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at some point you brought your family back from Rijeka to Novi Travnik, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. I brought my family back after the second conflict and negotiations, because I thought that the conflict between Muslims and Croats was over for good. In January 1993, I brought my family back to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the conflict, you and your family were in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, would you have sent your family away again had it been possible, and perhaps join them too after the conflicts resumed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, had the way through been open, I guess I would have sent my family away again, and a large number of people would have left too. But we were surrounded, so there was no way out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were surrounded once and for all, you simply could not leave the area as a civilian or a military or in any way.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Only as an exception, in agreement with the BH army, yes, some wounded could leave. They would be transferred to Split on a couple of occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Markovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few questions from Mr. Kordic. Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Markovic. My name is Stephen Sayers. I believe we met yesterday evening to discuss the facts that you know about this case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's accurate to say, Mr. Markovic, that during the three conflicts that you have described, June of 1992, October of 1992, and June of 1993, Mr. Kordic was only in Novi Travnik during the conflict that occurred in October of 1992; do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that he was present in the conflict of 1992, I mean the second conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was Mr. Kordic, in your experience, a political figure, a military figure, or both?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic was a political figure and a political figure only, in my view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, there has been some claim in this case that Mr. Kordic was actually the military commander of the HVO forces in Novi Travnik during the October 1992 conflict. Could you just tell the Court, who was the commander of the HVO military forces in your town during that time period, sir? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: During the second conflict, at that time the commander was Vlado Juric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the overall commander of the HVO forces in Central Bosnia in the October 1992, 1993, 1994 time period, sir, until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the military district was Mr. Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified, sir, that you were appointed to be chief of the defence office in Novi Travnik at some point. Was that a military position or a civilian position, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is a civilian duty. But I was at the same time responsible for coordination with the military wing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think that it's necessary to take up time with these exhibits, but we'd just referred the Court's attention to Exhibit Z345 and Exhibit Z577; the first exhibit being a recommendation to appoint Mr. Markovic to the position that he just described, signed by the Chief of the Travnik Defence Administration, Anto Puljic, and the second document being the actual decision making the appointment, signed by the head of the defence department, Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you became a member of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in Novi Travnik, Mr. Markovic, is it accurate to say that the brigade commander received his orders from the Operative Zone commander, Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that the brigade commander received orders from the commander, that is, Colonel Blaskic. After my term as the head of the defence department expired, I joined the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and I think it was the 21st of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any commanders in your brigade at any time, to your knowledge, ever receive orders from Mr. Kordic as opposed to the military commanders you've identified?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, when I was the head of operations and education, all documentation went through me, and there was never such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a circumstance in which Mr. Kordic had ever tried to give any orders to the members of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade at any time during the period in which you were a member of that brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard that. But I think that the chain of command was clear, so there were no problems there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the October conflict, Mr. Markovic, did you ever hear that the main road to the east of Vitez had been blocked by ABiH forces, specifically at the village of Ahmici, and that this blockade prevented reinforcements headed westward, HVO reinforcements, that is, from proceeding upon their way?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I learnt about it. I did not see it. But I learnt that units from Busovaca and Kiseljak were not allowed to go to Jajce, because we manned the front line at Jajce against the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, did you ever hear Mr. Kordic make any threats in relation to the village of Ahmici following this blockade incident on the TV or radio or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I neither heard nor saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever report to you or mention in passing that any such threats had been made in any of the media?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, sir, that there was a meeting at the Grand Cafe, or the Cafe Grand, in Novi Travnik during the October 1992 conflict. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At the Grand Cafe, on the third day of the conflict, rather the third night, when I pulled out - because my units were protecting the signals unit and some of the command had gone to the hotel, but I stayed behind to protect the signals - we pulled out to send the materiel to the old hotel, to the front line. That is where I found Mr. Kordic, Jozo Sekic, Marinko Marelja, and Colonel Filipovic talking. I saw them talking, but I was really too busy about other things, dealing with the front lines, so I know nothing about the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What was at the Cafe Grand? Did it fulfil any function other than being simply a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a coffee shop and a pizzeria in the true sense of the word. In view of the conflict under way, the municipal hall was on the front line itself, so that the whole administration had moved out. The civilian police and even all the municipal staff moved into that building where the civilian police was, in the lower part of the town. The Grand Cafe was the Grand Cafe, and it worked throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just a few questions in connection with the June fighting that you described. The fighting erupted in Novi Travnik in early June at about the same time that the ABiH had launched an attack on the neighbouring municipality of Travnik, resulting in the 20.000 or so refugees that you previously described; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is fair to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just give the Court an idea about the kinds of problems that were caused by this massive influx of refugees into your municipality from Travnik, sir? Just in general terms.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I can, yes. It was like an elemental force. More and more people arrived every hour, women, children, soldiers, just with basic necessities. It was general commotion, disarray, anarchy in the town. There were no police or anyone who could regulate it. We had a terrible problem because those people were breaking into flats, and they were saying quite frankly, "Well, I lost a house. Why don't I enter it here? You're protecting Muslims here." We had terrible problems there, but we simply were not able to prevent it. We tried to protect people as long as we could. We even accommodated people in our flats until it settled down, until life went back to normal. But there was complete anarchy during those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, noticing the time, I have about, I would say, five more minutes of questions. Do you want us to take a break or just to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That would be a convenient moment. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Markovic, we're going to adjourn for half an hour. Don't speak to anybody, please, about your evidence during the adjournment and until it's over, and that does include members of the Defence team. We'll be back, please, at half past eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, before the break, you were just discussing the impact of the influx of refugees into Novi Travnik from Travnik during the early part of June of 1993. One incident that occurred at around the same time was the Tuzla convoy or the Convoy of Joy as it travelled through Novi Travnik June 9th, 10th, and 11th. Were you in Novi Travnik at the time that the Tuzla convoy travelled through that municipality, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The suggestion has been made in this case, sir, that this -- the apprehension of this convoy by Croats in Novi Travnik was carefully organised, coordinated, and planned. Could you give the Court your perspective since you were there on whether that analysis or that opinion is a correct one or not.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is not correct. The convoy was spontaneously stopped by the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that you, yourself, sir, were accosted and insulted by an angry mob of people during this same time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at Nevic Polje. That is where one of the part of the convoy was stopped, and the other one was at the Vitez-Travnik intersection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few final questions, Mr. Markovic. You were asked generally whether you were aware of or had ever heard about any direct policy or indirect advocacy of plan or campaign of persecution against people of Muslim ethnicity or harassment of people of Muslim ethnicity. Did you ever hear Mr. Kordic making insulting or pejorative comments about Muslim people in any of the speeches that you heard him give in person or through the media?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I first heard Mr. Kordic speak at the oath-taking ceremony in Travnik and on that occasion he addressed the soldiers who were giving oath, and invited that we should organise together with Muslims against the aggressors and against the extremism of the Muslims, those who wanted to take over Bosnia and -- for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But did you ever hear him subsequently or at that time making comments of a pejorative or insulting nature against people of Muslim background or advocating violence against them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard him say anything like that. He talked about extremist individuals and such individuals were in our own ranks as well as among the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As Your Honour knows, coming on somewhat short notice of this particular witness, I may not be quite as well organised as otherwise. There may be gaps on what I hope won't be an extended cross-examination in any event. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask at the beginning so that I can understand your position. In the early part of 1992, what were you doing, precisely, in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I was the chief of a sector in the Bratstvo in charge of the peoples' defence for the whole corporation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware, of course, of the creation of the community of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Herceg-Bosna which incorporated Novi Travnik as one of its municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of it, but I was not actively involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, did this occur to you as an odd thing to be happening that a Croat-dominated organisation would be taking as one of its municipalities an area that had Muslims and Croats broadly in balance?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Croats and Muslims shared the power until the establishment of the HZ HB and then after that, the Croats pulled out of that. I think that this was in response to the actions by the BiH parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, what actions? The parliament was still -- was an operative government. Why, in an area where there were equal Muslims and Croats, should the Croats suddenly withdraw and cleave to or cling to a Croat-only type organisation. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was said that if -- because the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not functioning properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's be blunt. Was the or was a pre-concern of the Croats of Novi Travnik built on the fact that the factory in which you worked was so large and so important?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Novi Travnik was composed of 18 different ethnic groups. It was a multi-ethnic small town, and there were fewer Croats working for the factory than members of other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the factory and its strategic importance the reason why the HZ HB made Novi Travnik part of its community?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we see that for long enough, as opposed to separate units, one in Novi Travnik and one in Vitez, there was a joint HVO in Novi Travnik. Why was that, do you think?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not understand about the question. I did not understand about the joint HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vitez and Cerkez were run from where, Novi Travnik initially and then he moved to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were from Vitez and then they went back to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to the documents, if necessary, later. As to Mr. Kordic, did you by any chance read a newspaper article by a man called Cicak who spoke of Kordic forming a semi-military party in, amongst other places, Novi Travnik? He published this article or this article was published in March of 1992.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not read that article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Kordic been involved in military activities in Novi Travnik as early as March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that he never came to Novi Travnik as early as March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because we've heard from a witness called Zuljevic at page 22.606 that he met Mr. Kordic in Novi Travnik in March of 1992. Did you encounter him there as early as that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I said in my statement that I saw Mr. Kordic during the second conflict on the third night of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him there earlier in, for example, March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Since I was involved in military affairs, he may have come to see Mr. Jozo Sekic as a representative of HDZ for Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that he was only a politician, you've identified who you say were the military commanders, but who was commanding the military commanders so far as Novi Travnik was concerned?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: What period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March of 1992 and later. Start with March of 1992. Who was commanding, which politician was commanding the military commanders?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, military commanders did not receive orders from politicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you seriously saying that the military commanders are simply running everything themselves?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: We in Novi Travnik received our orders from Colonel Blaskic, and whether he was receiving his orders from others, I do not know, nor do I feel that I had to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because by the spring of 1992, your position was merely -- the spring of 1992 your position was what?
