utterances.text: Oh, I see, the Serbs. Thank you. Is it normal for the commander of the municipal brigade to inform his superiors of the fact that everything is all right in town?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is his duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the third piece of information on this page, do you recall Cerkez knocking at all doors and asking for the Bruno Busic Regiment to be taken out of town by all means?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that is what we asked Mr. Cerkez to do. And Mr. Jozo Sekic and I, the president of the municipality and I, we both asked for this because of all their excessive behaviour in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that none of you from Novi Travnik, neither the civilian structure nor the military structure, really wanted to have Bruno Busic in town?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't want them in town because there was no need for them to be in town. They only made the situation more complicated, as well as the interethnic relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say yes or no to the following: that at least one soldier of the HVO was killed by a Bruno Busic rifle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where are we going? You said a few more questions, Mr. Kovacic. That was a quarter of an hour ago. The witness has been giving evidence all day. Now, time is limited in this trial; that point has been made often enough. I don't know what the point of all this questioning is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm strictly within the issues which were raised during the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What issue? What issue is this related to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Bruno Busic was mentioned in this document, and it was my impression that the Prosecution was trying to imply that Cerkez is somehow commanding that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, have you ever made any such suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was asking whether the content of the letter reflected his having any authority to get the brigade out of town. That was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you've dealt with that. Now, Mr. Kovacic, let's move on. Let's have another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, indeed, I was just finishing with Bruno Busic. I have only one or two more simple questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Markovic, twice during your testimony while you were answering the Prosecutor's questions, you used the following words, that you simply carried out orders. Let me ask you the following: During your activity, regardless of whether this was in the office or in the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade later, did you ever obey an order which asked you to do something that was impermissible, for example, an attack against civilians?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, and I could not have carried out such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive such an order? Did you ever have one on your desk?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever issue such an order to anyone?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I claim with certainty that I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, thank you for coming to give evidence. That concludes your evidence before the Tribunal. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, our next witness is Mr. Dragan Grebenar from Vitez. The summary was distributed this morning. If you want me to inform you of the subject, I will, but I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Please take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed Your Honours? Thank you. Examined by Mr. Kovacic: Good afternoon, Mr. Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your name, your date and place of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I am Dragan Grebenar. I was born on the 25th of July, 1960 in Poculica, municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, I am married and I am a father of two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I am a chemical assistant, laboratory assistant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means secondary education?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But now you have your own company in Vitez, you have your business?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before the war, you worked for the SPS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, is it correct that sometime in the latter half of 1992, you were an active member of the village guards in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, in due course, also become the head of the village guards in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your village was ethnically mixed, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the population census of 1990, could you tell us how many Croats and how many Muslims were there in Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: According to the census of 1991 in the village of Poculica, there were 408 Croats and 330 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, with Prnjavor and Verhovine, Poculica made for one neighbourhood community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the ratio of Muslims and Croats in that community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: As you have said, the neighbourhood community was made of those three villages: Poculica, which was, as I have said, a mixed village ethnically, I mean. Prnjavor was purely Muslim, and Vrhovine which was also purely Muslim village. Also, according to the census of 1991, I think there were about 1.055 Muslims against 408 Croats in the neighbourhood community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You underline this term neighbourhood community. All of us who come from the former Yugoslavia have a problem to explain it. Is the neighbourhood community -- let us try to do it, was the neighbourhood community a formal political administrative subdivision under then regulations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, let me try to explain it like this, how I understood the neighbourhood community, and I think it is as you said. A neighbourhood community was set up under the instructions of the municipality, and the purpose of the neighbourhood community was to take care of the territories of the villages which make a part of it. For instance, before the conflict, before the war, a neighbourhood community was only engaged in social and political activities related to the betterment of life of villagers, that is construction of roads, water supply, and the rest to the benefit of all the inhabitants of a particular neighbourhood community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if I understand you properly, so that the citizens living in the territory of the neighbourhood community could solve together matters of a common interest for that neighbourhood community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, as a citizen of one such neighbourhood community, where the number of another ethnic group is twice as large as your own, did you ever feel any intolerance between the two communities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No. There was no intolerance between them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you worked for the SPS. There were members of both peoples in it. According to your knowledge, did the structure of the employees reflect more or less this population structure; would that be correct to say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, yes, it would be, but there weren't only members of these two peoples, there were Serbs employed there, even some Romanie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. But let us go back to the village guards in Poculica. When did they start to organise themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The village guards began to be formed in early 1992 or perhaps in mid-1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it self-organisation or did instructions arrive from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Self-organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did citizens organise themselves in village guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: For the simple reason that at that time, the Serb aggression was well underway from Vlasic, and quite simply some people had turned up who welcomed it all, that is, crime began to happen; thievery, robberies, so that people were frightened and scared and quite simply they were trying to take note of who was going through the village with what intent and things like that. If I may mention, Poculica is on the main regional road Vitez-Zenica which was quite a busy communication, and people were trying simply to keep track of who was moving around, especially since the former JNA was stationed in Zenica and Travnik and in other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, thank you. Mr. Grebenar, who appointed you the coordinator or leader of that -- of the village guards in your place? Did somebody appoint you? Did you appoint yourself? Will tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I didn't appoint myself. At a meeting, people, that is, the villagers, asked me to try to reorganise ourselves and that I should take over the leadership of the village guards to supervise a little this organisation and such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those who asked you to do that and suggested that, they were your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any representative of the authorities ask you to lead the village guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No. No authorities ever asked to form those village guards. We did it on our own initiative. We wanted to patrol the village, to keep it, rather, to keep an eye on it. And because I was one of the initiator of the things, one of the first to say that the village needed something like that so then they named me to become -- to be one who would organise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the village guards armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, at the outside we had two hunting rifles, two or three, maybe, and I believe that a neighbour had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to take a cross-section in time, could you perhaps give us the picture towards the end of 1992? Were you slightly better armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or perhaps a third period of time, indeed on the conflict of the 16th of April 1993, were you even better armed then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but even slightly better than the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you give us some estimate on the eve of the conflict on the 16th of April 1993, how many rifles did you have in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, I should say about 30 rifles altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all army rifles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No. They were hunting rifles and, yes, some army rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one more question about the village guards, I forgot to ask you something. Did a party, that is the strongest Croat party, the HDZ, was it perhaps actively participating in the organisation of village guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, on the 15th of April, 1993, did you learn in any way whatsoever or were you perhaps warned that an all-around broad confrontation might take place between the HVO and the BH army in the territory of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything that you remember that day? Did anything out of the ordinary happen for which that date stuck in your memory or was it a day just like any other?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned and as far as my neighbours are concerned, it was quite an ordinary day as any other day except that in Zenica, Zivko Totic, the commander of Zenica Brigade's escort, was killed. I think that four lads were killed in the locality called Podbrezje near Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But let's leave that because the Court knows about it. But anything else in your immediate neighbourhood? You didn't see any signs, anything that might indicate that there would be a confrontation the next day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that night between the 15th and 16th of April, 1993, did the guards discharge the faction as usual?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men did you have patrolling the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: That night, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone let you know that evening or perhaps during the night that you should be put on higher alert or that you should increase the number of guards or anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn and how -- when did you learn for the first time, and how, what was going on and what had taken place early that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: On the 15th, in the evening of the 15th, as usual when there were guards, since it was all on a voluntary basis so I somehow thought it necessary to be with those lads who were there and who are patrolling until about half past one. So I was with them until that time and then I went to bed back home. In the morning, sometime around half past four, I was aroused by two lads who were there in the central part of the village on patrol, and they asked me if I had any information about a possible attack by the Muslims from the direction of Vrhovine, Trahocice [phoen], and Prnjavor. I said that I knew nothing about it and whence that idea and had they noticed anything. They said they didn't notice anything out of the ordinary, but that a lady neighbour had invited them to her house, and told them that her sister who lived in the neighbouring village, Krtine Mahalla, had called her by telephone and told her, "Mare, are you out of your mind? How can you be at home still? There are stories here that there will be an attack on Poculica," and so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what those two guards who woke you up told you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I told them -- well, I realised that they were rather frightened. But before that, there were already such cases where somebody would notice something and then panic starts, but it has nothing to do with it. So I told him, "All right. Don't bother. I'll dress up and we'll go to Mare to see what is going on," and that's what I did. So we went to Mare Papic, that is, to her house, and I asked her. Then she repeated the story to me and she said that her sister was crying and asked her to get away, to go down to her, in her village or something. They asked me whether I could call anyone, whether we could learn something more about it. Since we already had the telephone numbers of the police and what I think was called the information centre and the telephone number of the command in Vitez, I dialed from that house in front of them, I dialed the command. The man on duty answered. He did not introduce himself to me. I did give him my name, and I asked, "Is Mario there? I need to talk to them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Mario," you mean Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, why did you want to talk to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Well, because of those down there who made up the command, Mario was the only one that I knew from before, because we worked for the same company, for the SPS. I thought it would be easiest for me to see with him, to see if he'd tell me anything, because I knew that he did have some duty, some post in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the man on duty tell you when you asked for Mario?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: He said that Mario was not there. "Can I help you," he said. I said, "Well, no, we've got some problems here." Then he asked me if we'd observed anything, and I said, "No, not really. But I need to talk to Mario." He said, "Well, I'll try to find Mario for you. Give me your phone number." So I left this neighbour's phone number, I gave it to him, and I asked him to try to find Mario as soon as possible so that he would call me back then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to Mario later that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Ten or fifteen minutes later, I believe it was, the phone rang. I picked up the receiver and Mario was on the other line. He asked me why I had been looking for him. I told him what the guards had told me and what the neighbour had told me. He said, "Very well. Did you patrol last night? Did you reconnoitre?" I said, "Yes." "Did you observe anything?" I said, "No." "Then please go on." Then he advised me that we should go on with observing some more and that we should report if we found anything that was out of the ordinary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, you said that he advised you. The advice that he gave you, was that a conversation between two acquaintances or between an officer and a person who was his subordinate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I consider that this was a conversation between, how shall I put it, two friends, because I felt I needed someone who had more experience, I needed some advice. I was not part of the military hierarchy and structure at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, can you please tell me, are you certain, or not at all, where did Mr. Cerkez call from? From his home, from the command post, or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never learnt that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I never did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you proceeded to observe.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: As I said, the two young men who were there - this may have been after 5.00, 5.10, 5.15, because at that time the watches were only until 5.00 a.m. and we did not want to go on with the shifts past that time - I sent one of the young men from the village to see whether the guards were still there. And with another one, I went to go look for those two men to ask them to stay there a little while longer, and I wanted to stay with them to watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were doing this, the village was still calm, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, had you already heard any explosions from other areas?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. When I reached the lower part of the village where I found those two young men, and as I was explaining to them that we should go on with the watch, we heard explosions coming from the direction of Vitez, from somewhere down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When can you say that the first shells were fired at your village, and from where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I believe that that was around 8.00 in the morning. They were aiming at my house, and my barn was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any casualties in your house at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear small arms fire starting from some part of the village following this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. I think that it was sporadic fire from Vrhovine and Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the fire was coming from the villages that were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the conflict, was there any army billeted there? Were those local people or people from outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: At first, they also had village guards which were exclusively composed of locals. But later, towards the end of -- in fact, in the middle or second half of 1992, some people whom we did not know appeared. For the most part, these were refugees. But there were also five or six men who were foreign, and we heard that these were Mujahedin. They wore different clothing too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these waves of refugees, especially at the end of 1992, were there people from Krajina, from Karaula, among them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where they came from. I know it was from the Jajce area. After the fall of Jajce, a number of them came from there. But I know that even before the fall of Jajce, there were some refugees in Prnjavor and Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with them, a number of soldiers also arrived.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shell that was fired on your house, from which direction did it come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I am not well versed in military strategy, but at that time we concluded that it must have been fired from in or around Preocica village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Preocica at that time was completely under ABiH control.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. They had the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you receive information on the arrest of Croat civilians in the upper part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I believe that this may have been as early as 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Nothing. I tried -- because at that time the shooting had intensified and the bullets were flying into the village, so we were scared. None of us had any military training or was mentally prepared for this. I asked for the opinion of others, what to do. They said that we should try to say that all those who were still in their houses in the middle section of the village should pull back to the lower part of the village where the rest of us were, and this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then at some point decide to evacuate to Krizancevo Selo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, but that was much later. It was 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me take you back to the time before you went to Krizancevo Selo. At some point during that day there was a public announcement that was broadcast from the minaret. What was that about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Sometime around 12.00, noontime, the PA system from the minaret was turned on and we were read -- or we were given an ultimatum that all Croats had five minutes to surrender their weapons and to gather in front of the school building and surrender there or else they would start killing everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any doubt to you that this call for surrender was referring to both the armed and unarmed population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: The announcement referred to all Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any doubt in your mind that this threat was against all Croats in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: There was no doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the response of the local population in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I can openly say that a chaotic situation ensued. People panicked. It was perhaps only then that I, too, realised that this was a real war, that this was real shooting, that people were shooting to kill. So we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us now, did you expect the arrival of UNPROFOR patrols? Because they had been patrolling.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, we did, which is why we had those telephone numbers at the information centre, so that we could call those numbers and so that UNPROFOR could intervene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the UNPROFOR patrol arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Some 40 minutes later, following the ultimatum, two UNPROFOR APCs arrived. They arrived at the lower part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, the part of the village where you were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your plan? What did you try to do with the UNPROFOR patrol?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: That was the time when the upper part of the village was, so to speak, cleansed of the Croat population. We were pushed back into the middle part of the village. And I expected that UNPROFOR, with their transporters, would go up there to the line of separation, that the shooting would stop and that we would try to calm things down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your plan to use this ceasefire to pull out civilians to a safer place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Believe me, at that time I was not thinking of a pull-back because I didn't think that it would be necessary. I thought that if UNPROFOR came, that everything would stop and that we would start to communicate again. Overall, I expected some kind of safety and protection from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did UNPROFOR eventually go up to the upper part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, they came back to the lower part of the village. Because while I was begging them to go up there, some 500 metres up from us, a shell fell. At that point, they turned around and went back to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, at the time when the UNPROFOR APCs were there, could it be said that the Croats were still lingering on in the middle part of the village where they were trying to offer some resistance, and in the lower part of the village where most of the civilians were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the attack went from the upper part of the village downward.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at around 1530 hours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Around 1530 hours, we eventually decided that we had to flee; civilians first, women and children. We concluded that it would be the safest if they went through a forest and through a creek, in the direction of Krizancevo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you reached this decision, did a person by the name of Vlado Ramljak come to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he come, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: At that time, that very moment when I was directing my family and others to that forest, Vlado arrived with tears in his eyes and scared, and he said, "Dragan, we have all been captured up there. My wife and children have been taken to Prnjavor. I was released and told to get you because they want you to come up there for negotiations, and if I didn't come back, they threatened that they would kill my wife and children."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do seem to be hurrying. Can you tell us, Vlado Ramljak lived there, and he came to you from the upper part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the ABiH had sent him as a messenger to invite you? That was the only purpose of his coming there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understood that, for all practical purposes, his family were kept as hostages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I said, "Vlado, just let me deal with the civilian sent them in the direction of Krizancevo Selo but there will be no problems. I will go up with you for these negotiations."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went to the upper part of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever arrive at those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, I did not because at that time, the -- we were seen, Vlado and I were seen from Sljivcica because it was an open area. So fire was open on us from some heavy weapons. I hid behind a house. Later I tried to run across. I went one way, and Vlado went the other side of the road. We separated but I was wounded and I never made it to negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, let's just clarify things. Sljivcica is an outcrop above the those three villages and in that sense it is a dominant feature in the area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. That is in the direction of Vitez. There is another dominant feature towards Zenica called Vjetrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the direction of Vitez, this is a dominant feature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is also dominant in relation to your villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you were certain, you were sure that ABiH had already taken control of that feature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that location, did they shoot, open fire on the village or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were wounded at that time. Is it true that you retreated from the village, wounded as you were, with other civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes. The civilians had left previously, but I was in a hurry. Two men gave me first aid and I hurried in order not to lose too much blood and then we joined up at Krizancevo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Still some people from the upper and middle parts of the village had been captured by the ABiH how many people remained in the village as captives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I did not know at the time but later, after the exchange, I received some data. It was about 70 civilians who ended up captured in Prnjavor. They were captured and they were detained in a youth hall in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the final figure, but earlier that day, is it true that some 50 people had been captured in the upper and middle part alone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then that figure grew up to 70 in the end?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were these people exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I believe that the exchange was effected about a month later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all people exchanged or did some die during the captivity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Not all were exchanged because some, and it was about a week after the attack around the 23rd, I believe, a member of ABiH opened fire and shot a burst of fire at the captives, and three of my neighbours were killed and several other people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who the perpetrator was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn whether he was criminally charged with anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I am unaware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other killings of civilians of -- in the area, have you heard of other such occurrences?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this was not an isolated incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the civilians were exchanged, did you also learn that men had been taken to perform engineering type of work for the ABiH army at the front lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody mention the conditions under which they had to work and the -- how they were treated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Perhaps an example will illustrate the best how they were treated. The Muslim forces had lost a soldier in an attack at Barin Gaj, and after that they tied up a Croat who was at the time about 60 years old. They tied him up with a rope and sent him down there to bring back the body of their killed soldier. It was in no man's land so he was tied up and they kept him at -- with a length of a rope and he had to go down there and pick up the body and bring it back to the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that firsthand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, from the person who experienced it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- were you ever mobilised into the Vitez Brigade or any other HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Listen, I believe that officially I was never mobilised, but after I was wounded, I was on -- I had a leave of disability.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your medical treatment when you came back, where did you go? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Following the treatment, I went to the front line at Kratine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I stayed there until the end of the war, that is until April 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your immediate superior there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: At that time, it was Ljuban Calic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there you were a member of the Vitez Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before your wounding and even before the conflict, did anybody ever tell you or showed by their behaviour that you were a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, among your immediate family or your next of kin, and I apologise for having to mention this, I'm not going to go very far --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Paragraph 2.10. We've heard evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Actually, I will not, but then I will kindly ask the Prosecution not to raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sure they won't. It's quite unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just, in closing, tell me one other thing: You had known Cerkez before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any opportunities to be with him in some social events or sporting events, things like that, celebrations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In company which included Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: It was rare earlier that the companies were not mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you notice that he had any leanings towards segregation in relation to any other ethnic group, especially Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mention him as a man who was -- who had any such leanings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, just one more thing: When you were at the front line, at Kuber Kratine line, did you ever receive an order to target any civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: No, I never received any such order. In fact, not even to target any military targets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your only task at that front line?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: My only task was to stay awake, to observe, and to try to defend. Because a number of times we were pushed back by a superior army. Our defence line moved about three times and we were already close to the village. We had nowhere to go, so our only task was to defend as best we could, and to stay as alert as possible. This was my understanding of these orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the Croat village was always behind you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in front of the village, ahead towards the enemy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the enemy was ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of the ethnic background of its members, because it was the army -- were they the enemy because they were the army or because they were some other ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR
utterances.text: I think -- I don't know how to answer this. They mentioned that they had Croats. For me, they were the enemy because they were attacking us, and whoever was in the army was our enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have you any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is exactly what I was trying to say, Your Honour, that Mr. Kordic's Defence had no questions of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The Prosecution can cross-examine in the morning. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Grebenar, would you remember during the adjournment not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include members of the Defence team. Could you be back, please, at half past nine tomorrow morning. We'll adjourn until then. 6
